Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Open opportunity triage and coverage balance — Q2 commit review

Tim —

Thanks again for the time last week. We are doing a quick internal triage of open opportunities that could move into the Q2 commit. To make sure finance has a clean forecast, can you please confirm stage and expected close probability for the line items below by EOD Thursday? Also flag any procurement/technical blockers we should surface to our CS/SEs.

- EHR Integration (POC complete) — current stage: Negotiation? expected close: May 15 — probability unknown
- Pilot Expansion (3 sites) — stage: Contract Review? expected close: May 31 — probability unknown
- Annual License (enterprise) — stage: Pricing approvals? expected close: Jun 10 — probability unknown

I attached a one-page snapshot of what we show in our pipeline (pipeline_snapshot_20290502.pdf). If you prefer, Monica can hop on a 20-min call to align details.

Goal from our side: get a conservative/most-likely commit figure we can fold into the finance forecast and a best-case number for coverage planning. If any of these will slip out of Q2, call it out explicitly.

Appreciate it —
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin

marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Marcus —

Appreciate the clean snapshot. Quick updates below (estimates):

- EHR Integration — stage: Final Tech Signoff completed today. Legal needs 3 business days to review the SOW. Expected close: 2029-05-10. Probability: 75%.
- Pilot Expansion (3 sites) — stage: Commercial terms being reviewed by procurement. They asked for a one-line T&Cs change; likely resolved this week. Expected close: 2029-05-24. Probability: 60%.
- Annual License (enterprise) — stage: Executive budget approval. This is dependent on internal Q2 reforecast; earliest close: 2029-06-12. Probability: 30% (likely slips to next quarter).

I attached the procurement note (Brightline_MA_plan.xlsx) for the pilot. Procurement is looped on the pilot but they requested confirmation of support SLAs and data residency options — happy to connect your CS lead if that helps.

Tim
VP of Digital Ops

Team — forwarding Tim's update. Key takeaways: EHR Integration looks solid (75% close, mid-May), Pilot at ~60% but procurement has a T&C ask, Enterprise license likely slips (30%).

Laura: can finance take the most-likely and best-case numbers and fold into the Q2 coverage recalculation? Quick math I ran locally (please verify):
- Most-likely: EHR Integration (75% of $140k = $105k) + Pilot (60% of $220k = $132k) + Enterprise (30% of $480k = $144k) = $381k
- Best-case (100% all): $840k

Rishi: any changes to deal strategy here? If pilot T&C is the blocker, CS can jump in to accelerate. Monica — please queue an SE to provide the data-residency SLA confirmation (Tim's ask).

We need a clean commit figure by Friday morning for the finance lock. If anyone expects numbers to shift materially, ping now so I can flag exceptions to the forecast.

Marcus

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the summary. A couple quick things:

1) Laura — please treat the EHR Integration at 70% for the conservative commit (finance prefers shaving 5 points when legal still has review). For the pilot, use 50% until procurement signs off.
2) Marcus — escalate the SLA/data residency answer; Monica, can you get an SE reply with explicit language we can provide to procurement? We should remove any ambiguity that would force procurement to push the pilot out.
3) If enterprise license slips, let's surface an alternate coverage plan to finance: can we accelerate any smaller footprint purchases (pilot add-ons or additional seat licenses) to preserve coverage? Marcus — compile a list of $50k+ movable line items by EOD Thursday and drop in the HubSpot deal.

I'll join Friday's quick trim call if needed. If finance needs a flagged exception list, call it out and I'll own escalation to the CRO.

Rishi
